title: The Open Boat

teacherSummary.text: After a steamer sinks, four men, the injured captain, the cook, the oiler Billie and the correspondent, row a ten-foot dinghy for thirty hours off the Florida coast. They see land and a lifesaving station, but no one comes. Taking turns at the oars, they form a quiet brotherhood. At last they run the surf; the oiler, the strongest, drowns. The survivors feel they can now be 'interpreters' of the sea's voice.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “NONE of them knew the color of the sky” slowly and put it in my own words: The four shipwrecked men in the small boat never look up, so none of them knows the color of the sky. Next, craft. I notice the sentence opens with a capitalized "NONE," stressing that all of them, without exception, are absorbed. My answer: The story begins with what the men did not know because they could see only the waves that might kill them; Crane shows that survival narrows the men's whole world to the next few feet of water.
